subject: [Triage] spike of self-serve credits to unverified .dev domains — action needed
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Unusual cluster: self-serve credits issued to *.acmeai.dev domains

Team — attaching a quick sample and the CSV. Observability flagged a surge in free-credit issuance tied to accounts using email domains under acmeai.dev and a few other newly-registered domains (see attachment). Summary: 138 grants in the last 12 hours, large overlap on UA strings and device fingerprints.

Quick asks:
- Can trust & safety triage whether these look like abuse vs. legitimate sandbox signups?
- If abuse, recommend we roll back credits and block the domain pattern from auto-issuance.

Attachments: suspicious_signups_20261110.csv (sample rows + device_fingerprint, ip, ua, granted_tokens)

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Security Analyst | Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:03:22 -0800
Subject: Re: Unusual cluster: self-serve credits issued to *.acmeai.dev domains

Thanks Ben — good catch. I pulled the first 50 rows and saw identical device_fingerprint hashes across distinct emails, which is a strong signal. Two immediate steps:

1) Pause auto-grant flow for email domains matching /.*\.(dev|test|local)$/ or the specific acmeai.dev pattern — Dev can you toggle the rule in infra?
2) Run a quick similarity clustering on password reset IPs and UA strings; flag accounts with >= 3 overlap indicators for manual review.

A few notes for the review: sometimes partners will use sandbox subdomains; Marissa, do we have an existing whitelist for Acme AI sandbox domains? If not, we should request a confirm from their ops contact before we whitelist.

Please reply with the tentative rollback list before executing reversals — we want legal & CS to have visibility.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Trust & Safety | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 14:28:10 -0800
Subject: Re: Unusual cluster: self-serve credits issued to *.acmeai.dev domains

On Tue, Nov 10, 2026 at 10:03 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Ben — good catch. I pulled the first 50 rows and saw identical device_fingerprint hashes across distinct emails, which is a strong signal.

Quick initial triage from infra:
- 138 new grants across 5 related domains; top one is acmeai.dev (72 grants).
- Rotation patterns consistent with disposable-domain providers (WHOIS age < 30d for many).
- 86% of accounts share one of three UA strings and two identical EC2-origin IP blocks.

I've temporarily disabled the self-serve grant rule for the matching domain pattern and queued a job to snapshot token consumption (see link). I also produced a candidate list of 42 accounts that meet the ">=3 signals" threshold; saved as flagged_accounts_snapshot.txt (attached).

Proposed next steps:
- Trust & Safety to confirm manual review targets (Naomi, Marissa).
- If confirmed, reverse credits and tag accounts with abuse=false/true accordingly.
- Keep a short customer comms template ready in case a legitimate customer is affected.

Dev
Dev Patel
SRE, Inference Platform | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:50:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Unusual cluster: self-serve credits issued to *.acmeai.dev domains

On Wed, Nov 11, 2026 at 2:28 PM Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Proposed next steps:
> - Trust & Safety to confirm manual review targets (Naomi, Marissa).

Filing a quick note: Acme AI (enterprise) sometimes points partners to sandbox subdomains (example: partnername.acmeai.dev) for early integrations. I exported a crosswalk of known Acme partner emails vs these flagged rows — attached as acmeai_crosswalk.pdf. Out of Dev's 42 candidates, 12 map to partner email patterns that we've previously seen in EAP requests.

Request: can we do a two-tier action — immediate rollback for the 30 high-confidence abuse accounts, put the 12 partner-like accounts into a manual review queue, and reach out to Lina Zhao at billing@acmeai.com / lina.zhao@acmeai.com to confirm sandbox mappings before acting? I can draft the outreach.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:42:13 -0800
Subject: Re: Unusual cluster: self-serve credits issued to *.acmeai.dev domains

Thanks everyone — good breakdown and conservative approach makes sense. Decision and instructions below: 

1) Action: Reverse credits for the 30 high-confidence abuse accounts immediately. Dev — run reversal and attach audit IDs to TKT-9142.
2) Manual review: Put the 12 partner-like accounts in a hold queue for 72 hours. Marissa to contact Acme ops (Lina) with the draft message; do not revoke credits for those until we hear back.
3) Platform change: Keep the temporary pause on issuance for acmeai.dev and add a rule to block newly-registered domains that match disposable-domain lists for 30 days post-registration. Engineering, please prioritize this in the next sprint.
4) Comms: Legal (cc'd) to review the rollback template. Customer support: prepare a short FAQ and a proactive notice if their partner accounts are impacted.

Ben — please upload the final list of reversed account ids and the forensic CSV to the ticket and include the attachment filenames in the audit log.

I'll follow up once legal confirms the message. Thanks for the fast turnaround.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Trust & Safety | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
